title: Steve Lewis's nasty songs, Bulldagger's Dream
summary: Williams recalls Steve Lewis singing risque songs for white people and in bar rooms but never at Black dances.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: What are these songs? Do you remember any of the songs?
Yeah, they used to sing Bulldagger's Dream, and Get Away From My Hope, Bet Y'all Don't
Want You No More, and oh man, several of them. What is the Bulldagger's Dream?
That was a song. He didn't give it that name. Yeah, well I've heard of it, but I never heard the words. Yeah, Bulldagger's Dream. Well I can't think of them.
I can't think of them words to that song man, but Steve could sing some of them. What was it about though? Just a woman, you know.

One of those? Like he had her, you know, that was his girlfriend, you know, you see. And he talked and then like he said, one of them songs he had, he said, let me see how he had it. So we was talking about that the other day up in the barbershop. Talk about Steve playing them magic song for them white people. Oh, get away, get away from my door. You're a big cock, oh I don't want you no more. And had it rhymed up, you know, going down the line with it rhymed up, I can't think I'm not staying so long. I was in the teens, you know, see when I heard him singing.
He wouldn't play them for colored people, huh? They didn't want to.

Oh no, they didn't. If he'd be in a bar room where they had a piano, you see, if he'd be in a tump where they had a piano, you see, then he'd play them, you know. Of course all them guys would like to hear them sing them, you know. But outside of that colored dance is nothing like that, no. He wouldn't do that. But if he'd get in a joint where they got a piano, a broken down piano, most all them bar rooms had pianos, and then, you know, see in a room where they could dance in the back, then he would sing them. Oh, that Steve was something, I'm telling you.
The Bulldogger's Dream, is that about a woman that's a freakish or something? Yeah, uh-huh.
That's one of them, what they call them? Thespians? Yeah. Yeah.
And I guess they would tell them about what you do.
Yeah, what you do, yeah. Oh, Manny, oh, that man had you rolling, laughing, rolling on the floor, boy, I'm telling you. Yeah.
Well that song was popular in New York way, way back then. Yeah. That Fats Wall and James B. Johnson and all those guys.
Oh, they used to sing it?
Yeah, and play it. I even have a record of it, but without the words. I have it down in my pocket. Yeah. They just call it the dream or something.
